t: This is Henrietta Street in Covent Garden. It was once home to a number of artists, and later became the location of many publishing firms. The street takes its name from Henrietta Maria of France, who was queen of England, Scotland and Ireland as the wife of King Charles I, from their marriage in 1625 until his execution in 1649. She was the mother of Charles the Second and James the Second. She didn't much like being called Queen Mary, and signed her letters Henriette or Henriette Marie.
